ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A simple harmonic transverse wave propagates along the positive x-axis with a wave speed of $10m/s$. Two particles, P and Q, are located along the propagation direction at coordinates $x_P=1\mathsf{m}$ and $x_Q=6\mathsf{m}$, respectively. The timing begins when the wave reaches point P, and the vibration graph of this point is shown in the figure.

1. What is the wavelength of the simple harmonic wave in meters?
2. After how many seconds does point Q reach its maximum positive displacement for the first time?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A simple harmonic transverse wave propagates along the positive x-axis with a wave speed of $10\,\mathrm{m/s}$. Two particles, P and Q, are located along the propagation direction at coordinates $x_P=1\,\mathrm{m}$ and $x_Q=6\,\mathrm{m}$, respectively. Timing begins when the wave reaches point P, and the vibration graph of point P is shown in the figure. 1. What is the wavelength of the simple harmonic wave? 2. After how many seconds does point Q reach its maximum positive displacement for the first time?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure is the vibration graph of point P, with the vertical axis y/cm and the horizontal axis t/s. At t=0, the curve passes upward through the equilibrium position y=0, first reaching the positive maximum displacement; at about 0.1 s, it passes through the equilibrium position again and goes downward; afterward it reaches the negative maximum displacement; at around 0.2 s, it returns again to the same phase as the initial one, "passing upward through the equilibrium position." Reasoning: From the graph, it can be read that the period for point P to complete one full vibration is T=0.20 s. The wave speed is v=10 m/s, so the wavelength is λ=vT=10×0.20=2 m. The distance between P and Q is Δx=6−1=5 m, and for the wave to propagate from P to Q requires Δt=Δx/v=5/10=0.50 s. Since point P moves upward from the equilibrium position when the wave arrives, the first time to reach the positive maximum displacement requires one quarter of a period, namely T/4=0.05 s. Therefore, the time when point Q first reaches the positive maximum displacement is 0.50+0.05=0.55 s.
